newsitem.title: CHINA: China's CATIC sets up firm for H-share listing.
newsitem.headline: China's CATIC sets up firm for H-share listing.

text.p: The Shenzhen CATIC Group said on Thursday it had set up a company incorporating the assets of several Shenzhen-listed firms for an H-share listing in Hong Kong.

Assets of the new company included a 52.24 percent stake in watchmaker Shenzhen Fiyta Holdings Ltd and a 68.34 percent interest in crystal display producer Shenzhen Tianma Microelectronics Co Ltd, Shenzhen CATIC said in a statement in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
The name of the new company, which also had stakes in five other domestic debt-limited firms, was given in Chinese as Shenzhen Zhonghang Industry Co Ltd.
Officials declined to comment on the new company.
The new company's assets were owned by Shenzhen CATIC before the move, which had been approved by China's State Council, or the cabinet, it said.
The statement gave no further details.

Shenzhen CATIC operates under Beijing-based CATIC, or the China Aviation Technology Import Co, which is owned by AVIC, Aviation Industries of China, a state-owned producer and trader of aviation-related products.
H shares are offered by mainland China-based companies and listed in Hong Kong.
Shenzhen CATIC is among the latest batch of state-run companies approved by Beijing to seek Hong Kong as well as foreign listings.
Shenzhen CATIC, which is involved in technology, trading, property, tourism and finance, planned to float only part of its assets on the Hong Kong bourse, an official said last month.
Trading in Fiyta's A and B shares and Tianma's A shares was suspended on Thursday morning on the statement and would resume in the afternoon, the Shenzhen Stock Exchange said.
